body.asks: One engine on this machine, the interface mounted to it over a socket, nothing polled: built at its smallest step on 2026-11-11, in site/host.ts. The stores attached read only, each taken again in turn as its ref moves, a failed read tried again; the home a folder of the host's own, held by one host at a time; the socket answering only the host's own Host and Origin, refusing attach and what is no message in words; the page told by its host, reloading only after an engine that had answered is lost, its addresses kept as paths so the home reads the same by any name of this machine. Left: the tools committing through the engine, once a change carries the head it read; on Linux a refs folder replaced whole is not heard until the watch fails; each renewal reads every block again rather than keeping what it held; every store is served to any origin, as before.

name: One engine, the interface mounted to it

body.asks: Weighed on 2026-11-11, as the author asked: Fable and Opus read the one engine side by side. Five faults both found; Fable alone the home rewritten between two names of this machine, shown from the home's own log, and renewals reading every block again; Opus alone two hosts writing over each other's home, and requests left waiting when the socket closes. Each found one grave fault the other missed: Fable's were not drastically more significant, and it is set aside for now, Opus reading in its place.
